findings.title: Plaintext passwords are written to logs on signup
findings.explanation: The PR description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields. It doesn't. In `src/lib/logger.ts`, `REDACTED_KEYS` contains only `authorization` and `token`. `password` is not redacted, so `logger.info('signup attempt', { body: req.body })` writes the user's plaintext password to stdout, along with their email and organization. Those logs usually go to aggregators and third-party services, with broader access and longer retention than the database. This also breaks the repo rule in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: 'Never log request bodies or headers on auth routes.' The line is also placed before validation, so it logs every attempt, including malformed ones and ones where a client sends the password under another key, such as `pass` or `passwd`. A key-based redactor can't reliably cover those. Remove the line.

findings.title: Debug failed signups by logging validation errors, not the payload
findings.explanation: The goal is to see why validation fails. Use `signupSchema.safeParse(req.body)` and, on failure, log only `error.issues`. Zod issues contain the field path and error code, not the submitted values. Optionally add the list of top-level keys received (`Object.keys(req.body)`) and the Content-Type. Return a 400 with the issues. Right now `.parse` throws a ZodError out of an async Express handler. That is probably an unhandled rejection on Express 4 and likely produces a 500 instead of a 400, which may be part of why failures are hard to diagnose.

findings.title: Redaction list is too narrow for a general safety net
findings.explanation: Even though the PR shouldn't log bodies, `REDACTED_KEYS` should at least include `password`, `password_hash`, `secret`, `cookie`, `set-cookie` and similar keys. That way a future logging mistake doesn't leak credentials. This is a separate hardening change. It does not make the logging line in this PR acceptable.

findings.title: Log is emitted for every attempt, including PII, with no correlation id
findings.explanation: Even with redaction, logging the email and organization for every signup attempt adds PII to the logs for little debugging value. If you need to correlate failures, log a request id and the validation outcome instead.
